page.m2197.text: Travel Genie Magic Toolbar | Security & Privacy

page.m2198.text: Learn how Travel Desk Genie handles Google sign-in information, Cloudflare account and subscription records, local travel tools, website storage and privacy requests.

page.m2199.text: Travel Desk Genie provides Travel Genie Magic Toolbar. This notice explains Google sign-in, machine registration, subscription administration and the documented desktop and website workflows.

page.m0247.text: What stays on the Windows PC?

page.m0248.text: Passport OCR and photo editing are documented as local tasks. Saved family records are described as protected with Windows DPAPI for the current Windows account. Use the application’s Export/Import feature when moving supported records; do not assume raw file copies can be read under another account.

page.m2201.text: What information does Google sign-in share?

page.m2202.text: The app requests basic identity permissions: openid, email and profile. We use your Google account identifier, verified email address and display name to identify your customer account, link machine access requests and provide account and subscription support.

page.m2203.text: Your Google password is entered on Google’s website and is not received by Travel Desk Genie. This sign-in does not request access to Gmail messages, Google Drive files or contacts. Signing in identifies you; machine activation, device approval and paid subscription access are managed separately. Signing in does not purchase or renew a subscription.

page.m2204.text: What does the Cloudflare service store?

page.m2205.text: Cloudflare Workers and D1 host the account and subscription service. Records include customer accounts, machine identifiers, device public keys and fingerprints, activation links, subscription status and expiry dates, and manually recorded payment amounts, currencies, receipt references and renewal history. The owner portal can also store internal support notes and account or access-security events.

page.m2206.text: Online access checks can record your public IP address, country, app version and contact times. Authorized administrators use these records to provide customer assistance, manage device and subscription access, investigate security issues and maintain renewal bookkeeping. A payment record is not an automatic bank charge.

page.m2207.text: How is information used and shared?

page.m2208.text: Google identity information is used for customer identification, account linking, access management and related support. Google processes the authentication flow, and Cloudflare processes the hosted account and subscription records. Authorized administrators can view relevant customer and subscription details for those purposes.

page.m2209.text: Account and subscription requests use HTTPS. The desktop protects its saved app session credentials using Windows user-account protection. During sign-in, the browser sends a short-lived response to a temporary listener on your own PC so the app can finish verifying your account.

page.m2182.text: Travel Genie Translate sends selected text to an online translation service. Do not send passport or customer information unless you have permission and your agency approves the service. A toolbar that prepares GDS text does not itself establish a booking-system connection.

page.m0252.text: Cookie choices, product ordering and chat preferences use browser storage. Chat messages are kept in session storage by the existing widget. The website has no passport-upload form and no installed analytics or advertising service. Optional analytics preferences do not themselves load a tracking provider.

page.m2210.text: How long are records kept, and how can I request deletion?

page.m2211.text: We keep account, device and subscription records while needed to provide the service, resolve support or security issues and meet applicable record-keeping obligations. Payment and audit history may need to be retained for those purposes. Requests to access, correct or delete account information are reviewed after verifying account ownership; we explain any records that must be retained.

page.m2212.text: Signing out or uninstalling does not automatically erase server-side account, subscription, payment or audit history. You can remove the app’s Google connection in your Google Account settings. Contact support to end Travel Genie sessions as well: removing the Google connection does not automatically invalidate all existing Travel Genie sessions or signed offline allowances. An already-issued offline allowance can remain valid until its expiry.

page.m2183.text: What should I send to support?

page.m2184.text: Send the product name, operating system, release version if known and a description of the issue. Redact screenshots. Do not send passwords, full payment details, passport scans or customer records through the public chat.

page.m2217.text: The optional support diagnostic export can be previewed before saving. It contains app, runtime and operating-system details and access dates; it excludes passport data, databases, raw logs, clipboard contents, customer email, machine IDs, tokens and keys. That export does not upload anything automatically. Email, chat or WhatsApp providers process the information you choose to send through them.

faqs.m0542.text: What is Travel Genie Magic Toolbar?

answers.m1508.text: Magic Toolbar is a Windows app for travel agents. It reads a passport and makes NAME, DOCS, CTCM and CTCE entries. It shows them for Amadeus, Travelport and Sabre. It also has F1–F12 shortcuts, reminders, a phone book, a translator and a visa photo tool. You check every entry.

answers.m1482.text: How does Magic Toolbar make a DOCS entry?

answers.m1509.text: Paste or scan the passport. Magic Toolbar finds the code lines at the bottom, called the MRZ. It checks the numbers and expiry date. Then it fills in passenger details and builds the DOCS entry for your GDS. If a detail is unclear, it stays blank until you fill it in.

faqs.m0544.text: What is the difference between CTCM and CTCE?

answers.m1510.text: CTCM is the passenger’s mobile number. CTCE is the passenger’s email address. Airlines use both to tell travellers about flight changes. They belong to the passenger, not your agency. Magic Toolbar writes each in the right format for Amadeus, Travelport and Sabre. It warns you if a country code is missing.

answers.m1458.text: Does Magic Toolbar issue tickets or connect to a GDS?

answers.m1486.text: No. Magic Toolbar only makes text entries. You check them and paste them into your own GDS. It does not search fares, hold seats or issue tickets. It does not connect to Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport. It is not part of any GDS or airline, so your booking work stays the same.

answers.m1460.text: How much does Magic Toolbar cost?

answers.m1488.text: Magic Toolbar costs $30 a month or $220 a year. The yearly plan saves you $140. Ask us for the lifetime price. You can start with a 3-day trial from the download page. Our team then turns it on for each Windows PC on your plan.

answers.m1462.text: Is passenger data safe with Magic Toolbar?

answers.m1489.text: Passport reading and photo editing run on your own PC. Family records you save are locked to your Windows account with Windows DPAPI. Only the translator sends text online, and only the text you pick. This website never asks you to upload a passport.

answers.m1464.text: Which languages does the Travel Genie website support?

answers.m1490.text: This website is built for more than 80 languages, such as Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Persian, French, Spanish, Turkish and Chinese. It picks a language from your browser and region. You can change it at any time from the language menu at the top. Your choice is saved on this device.

faqs.m1492.text: Magic Toolbar is for travel agents and ticketing staff who work in Amadeus, Travelport or Sabre every day. It saves typing on passport and contact entries. It also keeps daily tools like shortcuts, notes and reminders in one place on Windows. You stay in control and check every entry.

faqs.m1511.text: Is Magic Toolbar passport reading always correct?

faqs.m1494.text: No tool reads every passport perfectly. Magic Toolbar checks the MRZ check digits and marks fields that need a second look. Unclear or missing details stay blank until you fill them in. Always compare the result with the real passport before you copy any entry.

faqs.m1512.text: How do the F1–F12 shortcuts work in Magic Toolbar?

faqs.m1513.text: Open the Container Manager and save text you type often, such as fare rules, baggage notes or greetings. Give each one a key from F1 to F12, or Shift plus a key. Press the key and the text appears. You can sort texts into groups and back them up.

faqs.m1497.text: Does the visa photo tool guarantee approval?

faqs.m1514.text: No. The visa photo tool measures your photo against the size rules you pick, such as the 35:45 frame, head height and background. It explains any problem in plain words. Each embassy has its own rules, so always check the latest official photo rules before you send an application.

faqs.m1499.text: Can I move saved records to a new PC?

faqs.m1500.text: Yes. Use Export in the Families module, then Import on the new PC or Windows account. Saved records are locked to your Windows account with Windows DPAPI, so copying the raw file will not work. Export and Import is the safe way to move them.

faqs.m1501.text: Are the other Travel Genie products included?

faqs.m1502.text: No. Each other Travel Genie product, such as the CRM or the NADRA Visa Cross-Check, is a separate app. Each has its own page, release details and terms. Some are still being prepared, so their pages show what is confirmed and what is not yet.

faqs.m1515.text: What do I need to run Magic Toolbar?

faqs.m1516.text: Magic Toolbar runs on a 64-bit Windows 11 PC. Please read the User Guide before you install it. After you install, our team turns on the app for your PC as part of your plan. Each PC on your plan needs its own activation.

faqs.m1517.text: How do I get help with Magic Toolbar?

faqs.m1505.text: Use the chat on this website for quick answers, or message our team on WhatsApp. You can also send us an email. Tell us your Windows version, the tool you used and what went wrong. Please hide passenger details in any screenshot you send.

knowledge.m1741.text:
**Visa & passport photo tool**
• Drag guides to the crown and chin, or fit the head to 75% in one click.
• Straighten in 0.5° steps or rotate 90° to align a tilted photo.
• Improve a dull or soft photo with the quality enhancer.
• A checklist measures the final JPEG: pixel size, 35:45 ratio, file size, head height, centring and background.
• Problems are explained in plain words.

It measures against the configured specification but can't guarantee acceptance, so always confirm the issuing authority's current rules.

knowledge.m0624.text:
**CTCM: passenger mobile**
CTCM carries the passenger's own mobile number (country code + digits) so the airline can reach them about schedule changes. Magic Toolbar formats it per GDS and warns when the country code is missing.

**CTCE: passenger email**
CTCE carries the passenger's email address. Special characters are encoded the way GDS entries expect, e.g. @ is written as //.

knowledge.m0630.text:
**Passport → DOCS**
Paste or read the passport and Magic Toolbar fills the passenger fields, verifies the MRZ check digits and expiry, works out passenger type and title, and prepares NAME, DOCS, CTCM and CTCE entries for Amadeus, Travelport and Sabre side by side.
Passport OCR runs on your PC. Unclear details stay blank until you confirm them, so always review before use.

knowledge.m2306.text:
**F1–F12 shortcuts**
Container Manager lets you assign your standard text to F1–F12 and Shift+F-keys, so remarks, policies and greetings are one key away. Organise slots by category, mark favourites, see which slots are free, and export/import a backup.
Review each saved message before you paste it into a customer or booking workflow.

knowledge.m1092.text:
**Container Manager**
• Save standard text (fares, baggage, ticket policy, visa notes, greetings) in categories.
• Assign each container to F1–F12 or Shift+F-keys.
• Mark favourites and see which slots are free.
• Export and import a backup of all containers.

knowledge.m0648.text:
**Magnifier**
Select any area on screen to read small text clearly. The same magnifier feeds Travel Genie Translate: select a customer's message and translate it in one step.

knowledge.m0657.text:
**Travel Genie Translate**
• Select text anywhere on screen with the magnifier.
• The language is detected and translated into English.
• Fix anything misread and translate again.
• Type your reply in English and translate it into the customer's language.

Note: translation uses an online service (Google, as shown in the app), so the selected text leaves your PC.

knowledge.m0665.text:
**GDS Decode**
City, airline, country, car company, hotel company and aircraft-type decodes. Each task is shown for Travelport, Amadeus and Sabre in one row, with one-click copy and three text sizes.

knowledge.m0671.text:
**Instant Phone Directory**
Clients, agents and family members in one searchable list. Search by name, code, phone or note; copy a number, email or the whole record; group families; and import/export the list.

knowledge.m0676.text:
**Reminders & sticky notes**
• Today, Upcoming, Overdue, Recurring, Completed and Missed views.
• Each reminder has a category and priority; mark done, snooze, edit or copy from the same row.
• An alert appears when a reminder is due.
• Sticky notes stay on top, can carry a reminder and save automatically.

knowledge.m0684.text:
**Passenger families**
Keep repeat travellers and their families together. Saved records are protected with Windows DPAPI for your Windows account; use the built-in Export/Import to move them to another account or PC.

knowledge.m0692.text:
**More Travel Genie products**
Separate applications, not included with Magic Toolbar: NADRA Visa Cross-Check, WhatsApp Contact Number Extractor, WhatsApp Customer Observation Desk, CRM for All GDS, Amadeus Proposal Generator and Emirates Portal Sales Report Automation.
Full details are still being prepared. Ask us on WhatsApp for early information.

resources.m1521.text: Passport DOCS Entry in Amadeus, Galileo and Sabre

resources.m1522.text: How to enter passport details (SSR DOCS) in Amadeus, Travelport Galileo and Sabre, with examples, a format comparison and the checks to make before you end the booking.

resources.m1523.text: What is a passport DOCS entry?

resources.m1524.text: A DOCS entry sends the passenger’s passport details to the airline. It holds the document type, number, nationality, issuing country, date of birth, sex, expiry date and full name. Airlines need it for border checks. CTCM and CTCE are separate entries for the passenger’s mobile and email.

resources.m1525.text: How do I enter passport details in Amadeus?

resources.m1526.text: In Amadeus, add the passport as an SR DOCS element linked to the passenger with /P1. Fields are split by hyphens: type, issuing country, number, nationality, birth date, sex, expiry, surname and first name. Use three-letter country codes and dates like 12JUL85.

resources.m1527.text: How do I enter passport details in Travelport Galileo?

resources.m1528.text: How do I enter passport details in Sabre?

resources.m1529.text: How do the DOCS formats compare?

resources.m1530.text: All three systems carry the same passport fields in the same order. The difference is the command at the start, the separator and how the passenger is linked. This table shows the three formats side by side for one passenger, so you can compare them quickly.

resources.m1538.text: How to prepare a passport DOCS entry, step by step

resources.m1539.text: Work from the passport, not from memory. Read the details, check each field, build the entry in the right format and link it to the right passenger. Magic Toolbar does the reading and building for you, but you still check each line before you copy it.

resources.m1540.text: Scan or paste the passport into Magic Toolbar.

resources.m1541.text: Compare the name, number, dates and nationality with the passport.

resources.m1542.text: Fill in any field marked as unclear.

resources.m1544.text: Copy the entry into your GDS and check the response.

resources.m0892.text: What should I check for children and infants?

resources.m1545.text: Confirm the passenger type, date of birth and name spelling. An infant’s DOCS entry uses MI or FI as the sex code and is linked to the adult who travels with them. Age rules depend on the airline, so check them before ticketing.

resources.m1546.text: How should I handle passport reading warnings?

resources.m1547.text: Compare every field Magic Toolbar reads with the real passport. If a field is marked as unclear, fix it yourself instead of guessing. A correct MRZ check means the code lines were read cleanly. It does not prove the passport is genuine or that the passenger may travel.

resources.m1548.text: CTCM and CTCE Entry in Amadeus, Galileo and Sabre

resources.m1549.text: How to add passenger mobile (CTCM) and email (CTCE) contacts in Amadeus, Travelport Galileo and Sabre, with examples and the special characters each email needs.

resources.m1550.text: CTCM is the passenger’s mobile number. CTCE is the passenger’s email address. Airlines use both to send flight changes and delay messages straight to the traveller. Always use the passenger’s own details here, not your agency’s number or email, unless your workflow says otherwise.

resources.m1551.text: How do I write an email address in CTCE?

resources.m1557.text: How do I add CTCM and CTCE in Amadeus?

resources.m1558.text: In Amadeus, add each contact as an SR element linked to the passenger with /P1. The mobile number goes in full with the country code and no plus sign or spaces. The email uses the special characters shown above. Add both if the passenger has both.

resources.m1559.text: How do I add CTCM and CTCE in Travelport Galileo?

resources.m1560.text: How do I add CTCM and CTCE in Sabre?

resources.m1561.text: What if the passenger refuses to share contacts?

resources.m1562.text: A passenger can decline to share contacts. In that case, airlines expect a CTCR entry that records the refusal, instead of an empty booking. Ask the passenger first and explain why airlines want the details: they use them to warn about delays, cancellations and gate changes.

resources.m1563.text: What should I check before I end the booking?

resources.m1564.text: Check the country code, the number and the email spelling against what the passenger gave you. Make sure each contact is linked to the right passenger, not the whole booking. If Magic Toolbar warns that a country code is missing, ask the passenger rather than guessing it.

resources.m1565.text: Adult, Child and Infant Name Entry in GDS

resources.m1566.text: How to enter adult, child and infant names in Amadeus, Travelport Galileo and Sabre, with examples for each passenger type and the checks to make before pricing.

resources.m1567.text: How do passenger types differ in a name entry?

resources.m1568.text: An adult is entered with surname, first name and title. A child also carries an age or date of birth, so the right fare applies. An infant under two usually travels on an adult’s lap, so the infant is attached to that adult’s name entry.

resources.m1569.text: How do I enter adult, child and infant names in Amadeus?

resources.m1570.text: In Amadeus, names use NM followed by the number of passengers. A child adds CHD and the date of birth in brackets. An infant goes in brackets after the adult, with INF, the infant’s first name and date of birth. Add the surname too if it differs.

resources.m1571.text: How do I enter adult, child and infant names in Travelport Galileo?

resources.m1572.text: In Travelport Galileo, names start with N. and the surname. A child adds the age after *P-C, such as *P-C08 for an eight-year-old. An infant is entered as its own name with N.I/ and the date of birth, then linked to the adult who travels with them.

resources.m1573.text: How do I enter adult, child and infant names in Sabre?

resources.m1574.text: In Sabre, names start with a hyphen and the surname. A child adds the age, such as *C08, and an infant uses -I/ before the surname. Airlines also expect an SSR for the infant with the date of birth, linked to the adult who travels with them.

resources.m1576.text: The idea is the same in all three systems: surname, first name and title, plus extra details for children and infants. Only the command and the way age or date of birth is added change. Use this table as a quick reference before you start a booking.

resources.m1580.text: Can Magic Toolbar make name entries for me?

resources.m1581.text: Yes. When you scan or paste a passport, Magic Toolbar builds the NAME entry with the DOCS, CTCM and CTCE entries for Amadeus, Travelport and Sabre. You still check the passenger type, title and each line before you copy it into your GDS.

resources.m1582.text: What should I check before pricing?

resources.m1583.text: Check that each name matches the passport exactly, including spelling and order. Work out the child’s age and the infant’s age on the day of travel, not today. Age rules and fares depend on the airline, so check the price result before you ticket.

resources.m1584.text: Amadeus Commands Notes: Travel Agent Cheat Sheet

resources.m1585.text: A practical Amadeus cheat sheet for travel agents: availability, booking, names, contacts, pricing and decoding commands, each with a ready example.

resources.m1587.text: Amadeus command notes are a short list of the entries a travel agent uses every day: checking seats, booking, adding names and contacts, pricing and saving. This cheat sheet groups the most common commands by task, with an example for each one you can copy and adapt.

resources.m1588.text: Which Amadeus commands build a booking?

resources.m1589.text: A booking needs flights, names, a contact, a ticketing arrangement and a received-from line before you save it. Check availability with AN, sell seats with SS, then add each element. End and save the booking with ER, which also shows the record again.

resources.m1601.text: Which Amadeus commands price and decode?

resources.m1602.text: Use FXP to price and store a fare, or FXX to see a price without storing it. FQD shows the fares for a route. To decode codes, use DAC for a city, DAN to find a city code and DNA for an airline.

resources.m1610.text: Where are the Amadeus passenger entries?

resources.m1611.text: How can I keep these notes one key away?

resources.m1613.text: Travelport Galileo Commands Notes: Cheat Sheet

resources.m1614.text: A practical Travelport Galileo cheat sheet for travel agents: availability, booking, names, phone, pricing and decoding commands, each with a ready example.

resources.m1615.text: What are Travelport Galileo command notes?

resources.m1616.text: Travelport Galileo command notes are a short list of the entries a travel agent uses every day: checking seats, booking, adding names and contacts, pricing and saving. This cheat sheet groups the most common Galileo commands by task, with an example for each one.

resources.m1617.text: Which Galileo commands build a booking?

resources.m1618.text: A Galileo booking needs flights, names, a phone field, a ticketing arrangement and a received-from line. Check availability with A, sell seats from the display, then add N. for names, P. for phone, T. for ticketing and R. for received. Save with ER.

resources.m1625.text: Which Galileo commands price and decode?

resources.m1626.text: Use FQ to price the booking and see the fare. FD shows the fares for a route and date. To decode codes, use .CD for a city or airport and .AD for an airline. Always read the full response before you store or quote a fare.

resources.m1629.text: Sabre Commands Notes: Travel Agent Cheat Sheet

resources.m1630.text: A practical Sabre cheat sheet for travel agents: availability, booking, names, phone, pricing and decoding commands, each with a ready example.

resources.m1632.text: Sabre command notes are a short list of the entries a travel agent uses every day: checking seats, booking, adding names and contacts, pricing and saving. This cheat sheet groups the most common Sabre commands by task, with an example for each one you can copy and adapt.

resources.m1633.text: Which Sabre commands build a booking?

resources.m1634.text: A Sabre booking needs flights, names, a phone field, a ticketing arrangement and a received-from line. Check availability with 1, sell seats with 0, then add names with a hyphen, phone with 9, ticketing with 7 and received with 6. Save with ER.

resources.m1637.text: Which Sabre commands price and decode?

resources.m1638.text: Use WP to price the booking and WPRQ to price and store it as a price quote. FQ shows the fares for a route and date. To decode codes, use W/* followed by a city, airport or airline code. Read the full response before you quote a fare.

resources.m1644.text: Visa Photo Fixer: Size, Quality, Rotate and Align

resources.m1645.text: How to fix a visa photo for size, framing, quality and tilt with Magic Toolbar’s Visa Photo Fixer, and why no tool can guarantee embassy approval.

resources.m1646.text: What does Visa Photo Fixer do?

resources.m1647.text: Visa Photo Fixer prepares a photo against the size rules you pick. It shows crown and chin guides, checks head height and frame, straightens a tilted photo, improves image quality and checks the JPEG size. It helps you get close to the rules, but it cannot guarantee approval.

resources.m1648.text: How to fix a visa photo, step by step

resources.m1649.text: Start with the clearest photo you have, and keep the original file. Then work through the steps below in order. Fixing the angle and quality first makes the size and framing checks more accurate, and you avoid saving the image again and again.

resources.m1650.text: Open the original photo in Visa Photo Fixer.

resources.m1651.text: Pick the size rule for the country, such as 35×45 mm.

resources.m1652.text: Rotate and align the photo so the eyes are level.

resources.m1653.text: Use the quality enhancer if the photo looks dull or soft.

resources.m1654.text: Fit the head between the crown and chin guides.

resources.m1655.text: Check the background, size and file size, then save once.

resources.m1656.text: Can Magic Toolbar improve photo quality?

resources.m1657.text: Yes. The photo quality enhancer improves a dull or soft photo so it looks clearer before you check it. Keep changes light, because many authorities reject photos that look edited. It cannot add detail that was never there, so retake a blurred, dark or heavily edited photo instead.

resources.m1658.text: How do I rotate and align a tilted photo?

resources.m1659.text: Use the rotate and align tools to straighten the photo until the eyes are level and the face is centred. Then line up the crown and chin with the guides. A straight photo also makes the head-height check more accurate, so fix the angle before you crop.

resources.m1660.text: Which visa photo size should I use?

resources.m1661.text: Always use the size given by the authority that receives the application. Many countries ask for 35×45 mm, while the United States uses 2×2 inches. Rules also cover head height, background and file size, and they change, so check the official page each time.

resources.m1667.text: Many visa and passport forms, including Schengen countries

resources.m1671.text: Does Visa Photo Fixer guarantee approval?

resources.m1672.text: No. Visa Photo Fixer checks your photo against the measurements you choose and explains problems in plain words. Each embassy, visa centre and online system has its own rules and checks. Always compare the final file with the latest official instructions before you submit it.

resources.m1677.text: Setup takes a few minutes. Start with the five messages you type most, give each one a key, and test it in the app where you usually write to passengers. Add more keys later as you notice which texts you repeat during the day.

resources.m1678.text: Open the Container Manager in Magic Toolbar.

resources.m1679.text: Add a text you type often, such as a greeting or baggage note.

resources.m1680.text: Give it a key from F1 to F12, or Shift plus a key.

resources.m1683.text: What messages should a travel agent save?

resources.m1684.text: Save text you send many times a day: greetings, payment reminders, baggage allowances, document checklists, fare rule summaries and closing lines. Keep each message short and approved by your agency. Do not store passenger passport numbers or other private data in general shortcuts.

resources.m1685.text: Can I back up and move my hotkeys?

resources.m1686.text: Yes. You can back up all your saved texts from the Container Manager and restore them later, for example on a new PC. Keep the backup somewhere safe, and update it after you add new messages so you never have to rebuild your list.

resources.m1687.text: Translator for Travel Agents: Passenger Messages

resources.m1688.text: Translate passenger messages and replies in many languages with Magic Toolbar’s translator on Windows, and learn what to keep out of any online translation.

resources.m1689.text: How can a translator help a travel agent?

resources.m1690.text: Passengers often write in their own language: Arabic, Urdu, Persian, French or many others. A translator lets you read their message and reply in their language without leaving your desk. Magic Toolbar includes a translator on Windows next to your other daily tools.

resources.m1691.text: How to translate a passenger message

resources.m1692.text: Translate the passenger’s message first so you understand the request. Then write your reply in simple English, translate it and read it once more before you send it. Short, simple sentences translate much better than long ones full of travel codes.

resources.m1694.text: Translate it in Magic Toolbar and read the meaning.

resources.m1696.text: Translate your reply into the passenger’s language.

resources.m1698.text: Is it safe to translate passenger messages?

resources.m1699.text: The translator is the only Magic Toolbar tool that sends text online, and it sends only the text you pick. Remove passport numbers, card details and other private data before you translate. Passport reading and photo tools stay on your own PC.

resources.m1700.text: Should I translate GDS codes and names?

resources.m1701.text: No. Keep airline codes, city codes, booking references, names and times exactly as they are. Translation tools can change them or turn them into words. Translate the message around them, then check that every code and number is still correct before you send it.

resources.m0919.text: Travel desk shortcuts, notes and reminders: a practical setup

resources.m0920.text: Organize F1–F12 shortcuts, reusable desk content and reminders without confusing stored notes with live GDS commands.

resources.m0923.text: Shortcuts put frequently used desk actions within reach of a key. Magic Toolbar includes an F1–F12 shortcut feature alongside a container manager, notes, phone directory and reminders. Configure them around work you actually repeat.

resources.m0924.text: How do I organize command notes?

resources.m0925.text: Keep Amadeus, Travelport and Sabre notes clearly labelled. Separate explanatory notes from text intended for copying, and review instructions when your GDS workflow changes. Stored notes are a reference, not a source of live fares or a guarantee that an entry is current.

resources.m0926.text: What belongs in a reusable container?

resources.m0927.text: Use approved standard wording, internal checklists and reusable desk content. Keep sensitive passenger data out of general-purpose snippets, and confirm who can access the Windows account before storing customer information.

resources.m0929.text: Create reminders for follow-ups and tasks, then review them as part of your day. Desktop reminders supplement your agency’s process; they should not be the sole record for payment deadlines, ticketing time limits or other critical commitments.

resources.m0931.text: How to choose travel agency software for your daily work

resources.m0932.text: Compare travel agency tools by task, supported workflows, data handling, setup, pricing and support rather than unsupported feature claims.

resources.m0935.text: Travel agency software supports business tasks such as passenger records, customer follow-ups, quotations and reporting. A booking portal, a CRM and a desktop productivity toolbar solve different problems. Choose by the work you need to complete, not by a long list of feature names.

resources.m0937.text: Write down your recurring task, required input, expected output and systems involved. Ask for a demonstration using synthetic data. Check operating systems, actual integrations, review steps and failure handling. A claim of compatibility should be supported by a documented workflow.

resources.m0938.text: What should I check about customer data?

resources.m0939.text: Identify what is stored, where it is stored, who can access it and which services receive it. Ask about export, deletion and retention. Do not assume that every product in one brand has identical data handling.

resources.m0940.text: What should I check before paying?

resources.m0941.text: Confirm the plan, billing period, activation method, device limits, refund terms and support route. Magic Toolbar lists $30 monthly and $220 yearly in USD; lifetime terms are by enquiry. Separate specialist products have their own release status and terms.

resources.m0942.text: Is Magic Toolbar a booking portal?

resources.m0943.text: No. Magic Toolbar prepares entries and brings Windows desk tools together. It does not search live inventory, hold seats or issue tickets. The separate online-platform concepts in the catalogue have no confirmed public booking or payment capabilities.
